Uwasilishaji wa Makala Ikisiri Makala hii inachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo wa istilahi za Kiingereza katika Kiswahili na athari zake kwa kuangazia uga wa biolojia, fizikia na kemia kupitia vidahizo teule vya Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia na kemia (2012).
Azma kuu ya uchunguzi huu ni kutathmini mchango wa tafsiri mkopo wa msamiati wa Kiingereza katika suala zima la kukuza lugha ya Kiswahili.
Kwa mujibu wa makala hii eneo hili halijapewa aula miongoni mwa mada mbalimbali za tafsiri zilizokwishachunguzwa.
Hii imemuhamasisha mtafiti kulishughulikia eneo hili.
Data ya makala hii ilikusanywa uwandani katika idara na taasisi zilizo katika jiji la Dar es Salaam kwa njia ya usaili, hojaji na chanzo cha data cha maktabani.
Idara na taasisi zilizohusishwa katika ukusanyaji wa data ni: Idara ya Lugha za Kigeni na Isimu, TATAKI kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam pamoja na BAKIZA.
Idara na taasisi hizi zinapatikana mkoani Dar es Salaam Wilaya ya Ubungo ambapo mtafiti alifanikiwa kudodosa na kufanya mahojiano ya ana kwa ana kwa wataalamu wa tafsiri.
Aidha, data ilikusanywa kutoka katika matini mbalimbali kutoka chanzo cha data cha maktabani.
Mathalani, kamusi, tasinifu, majarida na vitabu kadhaa kulingana na mada ya makala hii.
Malengo ya makala hii yametimizwa kwa kuongozwa na Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi iliyoasisiwa na Kiingi (1989) na kuendelezwa na Kiingi (1992) na Kiingi (1998) na Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001).
Halikadhalika, data ya makala hii imechambuliwa kwa kutumia mkabala wa maelezo.
Aidha, matokeo yameonesha kuwa Kiswahili kimejipatia istilahi lukuki katika tasnia ya biolojia, fizikia pamoja na kemia kupitia mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo.
Makala hii ni muhimu kwa wanaisimu kwani inabainisha istilahi mbalimbali za lugha ya Kiingereza katika uwanja wa biolojia, fizikia pamoja na kemia zilizoingizwa katika Kiswahili kupitia tafsiri mkopo.
Inapendekezwa kuwa watafiti wa lugha wachunguze njia nyinginezo za ukopaji zinazokiendeleza Kiswahili kama vile utohozi na uasilishaji.

Utangulizi Tafsiri ni tendo la kuhawilisha ujumbe ulio katika maandishi kutoka lugha chanzi kwenda katika lugha pokezi bila kuathiri maana iliyokusudiwa katika lugha chanzi.
Hivyo, tafsiri huchukuliwa kama mbinu ya kujifunza lugha za kigeni, kuonesha tamaduni mbalimbali, ujuzi na maarifa ya jamii nyingine kama vile taarifa za maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia.
Raghba inayomsukuma mtu kutafsiri ujumbe uliyomo katika lugha chanzi kwenda lugha pokezi ni kutaka kuwezesha mawasiliano miongoni mwa wazungumzaji wa lugha zinazotofautiana.
Tunaweza kusema kuwa tafsiri ni njia au hata daraja la kuleta pamoja jamii kadha wa kadha zinazozungumza lugha zenye kutofautiana.
Aidha, tafsiri mkopo ni mojawapo ya njia ya kuunda msamiati mpya ambapo dhana ya lugha chanzi huchukuliwa na kutafsiriwa katika lugha lengwa kwa mfano, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau na kadhalika.
Mkakati wa ukopaji kupitia tafsiri mkopo umeshika kasi kutokana na maendeleo makubwa yanayojitokeza katika medani ya sayansi na teknolojia pamoja na jamii kukua katika usasa hivyo kuwa na uhitaji mkubwa wa msamiati wa kuelezea dhana mbalimbali.
Mtafiti wa makala hii anachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo wa msamiati wa Kiingereza katika Kiswahili.
Mtafiti amejikita katika uwanja wa biolojia, fizikia pamoja na kemia kupitia vidahizo teule vya kamusi ya biolojia, fizikia na kemia (2012).
Azma kuu ni kutathmini mchango wa tafsiri mkopo wa msamiati wa Kiingereza katika suala zima la kukuza lugha ya Kiswahili.
Kazi za tafsiri zimekuwa zikifanyika mara kadhaa ulimwenguni (Mwansoko, 1996, Malangwa, 2005, Giambruno, 2008, Baker & Saldanha, 2008, Malangwa, 2010, Malangwa, 2014).
Crystal (2002) anafafanua kuwa teknolojia mpya aghalabu huwa na athari kwa lugha, iwe ni ya maandishi au ya mazungumzo.
Hii ndiyo sababu ya lugha ya Kiingereza kukiathiri Kiswahili kileksikolojia.
Aidha, Crystal (2004) anaona kuwa athari kubwa kwa maendeleo ya kileksia ya Kiswahili imetokana na Kiingereza ambayo ni lugha kuu ya Teknolojia ya Habari na Mawasiliano pamoja na Kiarabu.
Mwaro-Were (2000) pamoja na Adika na Kevogo (2014) wanaeleza kuwa tangu enzi na enzi, mikopo ya kileksia imekuwa na ushawishi mkubwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili.
Kileksikolojia, lugha za kigeni kadhaa zimeathiri Kiswahili kwa viwango tofauti.
Baadhi ya lugha hizo ni Kireno, Kiajemi, Kiarabu, Kihindi, Kijerumani na Kiingereza.
Hii inadhihirisha wazi kuwa maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia yameleta athari kubwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili.
Tafsiri ina dhima ya kukuza na kueneza lugha hasa kupitia ule mchakato wa kuhamishia miundo ya misemo ya lugha chanzi kwenye lugha lengwa.
Pia, tafsiri ni liwazo kwa mfasiri anapofanikiwa kukamilisha kazi yake kwa ufanisi (Mwansoko, 2016).
Nassor (2017) kwa upande wake anaeleza kuwa kasi ya kuunda istilahi za Kiswahili imekuwa kubwa katika miaka ya hivi karibuni tofauti na ile ya miaka ya 1960.
Anaongeza kwa kusema kuwa mwishoni mwa karne ya 19 jamii ya Waswahili ilipokea maendeleo makubwa ya sayansi na teknolojia pamoja na nyanja nyinginezo.
Kutokana na hali hii lugha ya Kiswahili imepokea mabadiliko makubwa.
Hivyo, juhudi za uendelezaji wa lugha ya Kiswahili kiistilahi zilishamiri ili kuweza kwenda sawia na maendeleo hayo.
Sambamba na tafiti hizi zinazochunguza maendeleo ya lugha ya Kiswahili kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia, makala hii pia inalishughulikia hilo isipokuwa imejikita katika uwanja wa tafsiri mkopo mahususi kwa upande wa biolojia, fizikia na kemia.
Adolph (2019) kwa upande wake amechunguza istilahi za fani ya tiba na kompyuta zenye asili ya Kiingereza katika Kiswahili na michakato yake ya utohozi.
Matokeo ya utafiti wake yanathihirisha wazi kuwa Kiswahili kimekuwa kimsamiati kutokana na utohozi wa istilahi za tiba na kompyuta kutoka Kiingereza.
Hivyo, utohozi huo umekifanya Kiswahili kukua kutokana na ongezeko kubwa la msamiati wa sayansi na teknolojia katika upande wa kompyuta na tiba.

Kigezo kimojawapo cha kukua na kubadilika kwa lugha ni kuongezeka kwa istilahi.
Kwa mujibu wa Adolph (2019) ni kwamba ili istilahi ziongezeke katika lugha lazima ziundwe istilahi mpya.
Lugha huundiwa istilahi ili utamaduni wake ukidhi dhana ambazo hapo awali zilikuwa hazimo katika utamaduni huo.
Andiko hili ni muhimu sana katika makala hii kwani linaonesha ni kwa namna gani lugha hukua na kukidhi haja ya mawasiliano miongoni mwa wanajamii.
Makala hii inachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo wa istilahi za Kiingereza katika Kiswahili na athari zake kwa kuangazia uga wa biolojia, fizikia na kemia tofauti na utafiti wa Adolph (2019) unaochunguza ukuaji wa lugha ya Kiswahili kupitia utohozi wa istilahi za tiba na kompyuta.
Wataalamu wengi walioshughulikia ukopaji wanakubaliana kwa pamoja kuwa ukopaji ni uhamishaji wa vipengele vya kileksika kutoka lugha moja kwenda lugha nyingine (Haugen, 1950; Polomé, 1980; Adolph, 2014; Winford, 2003).
Makala hii imegawanyika katika sehemu tano: Sehemu ya kwanza ni utangulizi ambamo inaelezwa dhana ya tafsiri kwa ujumla na dhima zake pamoja na dhana ya tafsiri mkopo.
Sehemu ya pili inafafanua nadharia iliyoongoza uchambuzi wa data ya makala hii.
Sehemu ya tatu inaelezea methodolojia.
Sehemu ya nne ni uchambuzi wa data kuhusu mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo kutoka lugha ya Kiingereza kuja Kiswahili na athari zake.
Mjadala unahusiana na istilahi za nyanja za biolojia, fizikia na kemia kutoka katika kamusi ya biolojia, fizikia na kemia (2012).
Sehemu ya tano ni hitimisho.
Nadharia Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi imetumika ili kutupatia data ya makala hii.
Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi inafungamanishwa na Kiingi (1989) ambaye ndiye mwanzilishi wa kwanza wa nadharia hii.
Baadaye nadharia hii iliendelezwa na Kiingi (1992, 1998); Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001); Kevogo, Mukuthuria, na Ontieri, (2018); Kevogo (2020).
Nadharia hii ina vigezo vya kisayansi vya istilahi faafu vyenye dhima kuu katika tathmini inayofanywa katika makala yetu.
Wataalamu kadhaa mathalan Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008), wameweka bayana misingi anuwai inayopaswa kufuatwa wakati wa ukopaji, utohoaji na uundaji wa istilahi za lugha za kienyeji na zile za kigeni katika Kiswahili.
Misingi hiyo inajibainisha katika Tumbo-Massabo na Mwansoko (2008).
Nayo ni kuunda istilahi kwa kutumia: Kiswahili, Lugha za Kibantu, Lugha nyingine za Afrika na Lugha za kigeni.
Pamoja na maoni mengine mengi ya Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (1997) juu ya misingi hiyo, wanapendekeza misingi ifuatayo: Istilahi yafaa ziakisi sifa bainifu za dhana zinazoziwakilisha (au angalau zidokeze hali hiyo) na ziwe angavu kwa watumiaji wanaolengwa; Endapo istilahi zitaundwa kwa kutumia mbinu za muungano na mwambatano wa maneno, basi mambo yafuatayo itabidi yazingatiwe:
Idadi ya maneno yanayounganishwa au yanayoambatanishwa yafaa yasizidi mawili.
Vistari visitumiwe kutenga istilahi ambatani, kwani katika Kiswahili istilahi za namna hii kwa kawaida hutamkwa kama neno moja, lenye mkazo mkuu kwenye silabi moja tu.
Kwa mfano: -zao mtiririko; na -nusu kipenyo; Istilahi za namna hii yafaa zisiwe na silabi zaidi ya nne, kwani kwa kawaida maneno ya Kiswahili yana wastani wa kati ya silabi moja na tano tu.
Istilahi sharti ziwe na uwezo mkubwa wa kunyambuliwa ili ziweze kuzalisha istilahi nyingine za kikoa au ukanda unaohusika.
Hii itawezesha istilahi zinazowakilisha dhana zinazokaribiana kimaana au zinazotokana na shina moja kuonesha kimantiki ukaribiano huo.
Kwa mfano: taifa, taifisha, utaifa, -a kitaifa, -sio na taifa na -siyo wa taifa.

Istilahi (hasa zile zenye vivuli vya maana vinavyoingiliana) sharti ziwe na ulinganifu wa mtiririko.
Istilahi zifuatazo, kwa mfano, zinaonesha ulinganifu wa mtiririko unaokubalika: Tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko tabakakati na kadhalika.
Istilahi sharti ziwe toshelevu, yaani ziakisi sifa za dhana zinazoziwakilisha (na siyo, mathalani kupingana nazo) kwa mfano, istilahi: tahakiki ya maandishi si mwafaka kwa sababu inamaanisha uhakiki wa maandishi kwa jumla badala ya uhakiki au uchambuzi wa fasihi.
Istilahi lazima ziwe fupi na zenye kueleweka.
Istilahi ndefu kama vile majira ya majani kupukutika (kipupwe kinapokaribia) hazifai kwani hazizingatii msingi wa iktisadi ya lugha.
Misingi hii ni ya muhimu katika uundaji wa istilahi kwani inatoa dira ya nini kifanyike katika suala zima la utohoaji, uundaji na ukopaji.
Aidha, zimependekezwa njia za uundaji wa istilahi.
Tuangalie njia hizo hapa chini: mosi, kutafsiri, hasa kutoka kwenye lugha ambazo zinajulikana kuwa ni za kimataifa mathalani, Kiingereza, Kifaransa, Kihispania na kadhalika.
Pili, kuunda istilahi kutokana na mifumo ya dhana.
Nadharia hii ni faafu kwani imetupatia misingi ya kufuata wakati wa kufanaya mchakato wa kutafsiri.
Halikadhalika, imeweka wazi suala la njia za uundaji wa istilahi.
Methodolojia Kila mtafiti hutumia mbinu faafu na bayana kwa utafiti wake.
Makala hii ni matokeo ya utafiti wa kitaamuli uliofanyikia maktabani na uwandani.
Mtafiti amekusanya data kutoka katika Idara ya Lugha za Kigeni na Isimu, TATAKI kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam pamoja na BAKIZA mkoani Dar es Salaam Wilaya ya Ubungo ambako data ilikusanywa kwa mbinu ya usaili, hojaji na chanzo cha data cha maktabani.
Kwa mujibu wa Krishnaswami na Ranganatham (2005) usaili ni mbinu ya ukusanyaji data ambayo huhusisha majibizano baina ya mtafiti na mtafitiwa kwa lengo la kupata taarifa zinazohusiana na mada inayoshughulikiwa.
Kupitia mbinu ya usaili mtafiti alifanikiwa kufanya mahojiano ya ana kwa ana na wataalamu wa tafsiri kutoka idara na taasisi zilizobainishwa hapo juu.
Hojaji huandaliwa kwa lengo la kukusanya taarifa muhimu kutoka kwa watafitiwa (Mugenda na Mugenda, 2003).
Mbinu ya hojaji inaweza kufanyika ama kwa njia ya ana kwa ana au kwa njia isiyokuwa ya ana kwa ana kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia.
Maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia yamekuwa kichocheo cha hojaji mbalimbali kuweza kutumwa na mtafiti kwa watafitiwa wake kielektroniki (wavuti na baruapepe).
Hata hivyo, mtafiti wa makala hii ametumia njia ya hojaji ya ana kwa ana kwani watoa taarifa walikuwa eneo moja na linalofikika kiurahisi.
Aidha, mtafiti amesoma maandiko mbalimbali mathalani majarida, tasinifu, kamusi nakadhalika kutoka katika chanzo cha data cha maktabani.
Matokeo ya Utafiti Matokeo ya makala hii yamepatikana baada ya uchunguzi na uchambuzi wa data kuhusu ukuaji wa Kiswahili kupitia istilahi za tafsiri mkopo kutoka lugha ya Kiingereza.
Tafsiri mkopo ni mbinu ya uundaji wa istilahi inayohusisha uhawilishaji wa neno kwa neno kwa kipengele cha kimuundo na dhana kwa ujumla.
Muundo wa istilahi zilizoundwa kutokana na mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo hubadilika ili ulingane na kanuni za kimofolojia na kifonolojia za lugha pokezi.
Kutokana na mbinu ya usaili, hojaji na chanzo cha data cha maktabani, imebainika kuwa istilahi kadhaa kutoka nyanja za biolojia, fizikia na kemia kupitia kamusi ya biolojia, fizikia na kemia (2012) zimeingizwa katika Kiswahili kutoka Kiingereza kwa kupitia mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo.
Mifano ifuatayo inathibitisha kauli hii:
Tafsiri Mkopo katika Uwanja wa Biolojia Kupitia mbinu ya usaili, hojaji na chanzo cha data cha maktabani, imethibitika kuwa Kiswahili kimejipatia istilahi zinazohusiana na uwanja wa biolojia kupitia mkakati wa tafsiri mkopo.

Article Submission Abstract
This article examines the loan translation strategy of English terminology in Kiswahili and its effects by focusing on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through selected entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The main aim of this investigation is to assess the contribution of the loan translation of English vocabulary to the overall development of the Kiswahili language. According to this article, this area has not been prioritized among the various translation topics that have already been studied. This has motivated the researcher to address this area. The data for this article was collected in the field from departments and institutions located in the city of Dar es Salaam through interviews, questionnaires, and library-based data sources. The departments and institutions involved in data collection are: the Department of Foreign Languages and Linguistics, TATAKI from the University of Dar es Salaam, as well as BAKIZA. These departments and institutions are located in Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam Region, where the researcher was able to conduct inquiries and hold face-to-face interviews with translation experts. In addition, data was collected from various texts from the library data source. For instance, dictionaries, dissertations, journals, and several books were used, depending on the subject of this article. The objectives of the article have been achieved by being guided by the Theory of Scientific Terminology pioneered by Kiingi (1989) and further developed by Kiingi (1992) and Kiingi (1998), as well as Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001). Likewise, the data for this article was analyzed using a descriptive approach. In addition, the findings have shown that Kiswahili has acquired numerous terminologies in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through the loan translation strategy. This article is important for linguists as it identifies various English-language terminologies in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry that have been incorporated into Kiswahili through loan translation. Introduction  
Translation is the act of transferring a message contained in writing from the source language to the target language without altering the intended meaning in the source language. Thus, translation is regarded as a method of learning foreign languages, showcasing various cultures, and transmitting the knowledge and skills of other communities, such as information on scientific and technological advancements. The motivation that drives a person to translate the message from the source language to the target language is the desire to facilitate communication among speakers of different languages. We can therefore say that translation is a means or even a bridge to bring together various communities that speak different languages. Moreover, loan translation is one method of coining new vocabulary, where a concept from the source language is adopted and translated into the target language; for example, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, and so on. The strategy of borrowing through loan translation has gained momentum due to the significant developments occurring in the field of science and technology, coupled with society’s advancement into modernity, resulting in a high demand for vocabulary to describe various concepts. The researcher of this article investigates the loan translation strategy of English vocabulary into Kiswahili. The researcher has focused on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through selected entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The main objective is to evaluate the contribution of loan translation of English vocabulary to the overall development of the Kiswahili language. Translation work has been carried out numerous times around the world (Mwansoko, 1996; Malangwa, 2005; Giambruno, 2008; Baker & Saldanha, 2008; Malangwa, 2010; Malangwa, 2014). Crystal (2002) explains that new technology often has an impact on language, whether written or spoken. This is the reason why the English language has influenced Swahili at the lexical level. Furthermore, Crystal (2004) observes that the greatest influence on the lexical development of Swahili has come from English, which is the main language of Information and Communication Technology, as well as from Arabic. Mwaro-Were (2000), along with Adika and Kevogo (2014), explain that since ancient times, lexical borrowing has had a significant influence on the Swahili language. Lexicologically, several foreign languages have influenced Swahili to varying degrees. Some of these languages are Portuguese, Persian, Arabic, Hindi, German, and English. This clearly demonstrates that advancements in science and technology have had a significant impact on the Swahili language. Translation plays a role in promoting and spreading a language, especially through the process of transferring structural expressions from the source language to the target language. Additionally, translation brings satisfaction to the translator when they successfully complete their work effectively (Mwansoko, 2016). Nassor (2017), for his part, explains that the rate of coining Swahili terminology has increased significantly in recent years compared to the 1960s. He further adds that at the end of the 19th century, the Swahili community experienced major advancements in science and technology, as well as in other fields. As a result, the Swahili language has undergone significant changes. Therefore, efforts to develop Swahili terminologically intensified in order to keep pace with these advancements. Alongside studies that examine the development of the Swahili language due to advancements in science and technology, this article also addresses this issue but focuses specifically on the field of loan translation in the areas of biology, physics, and chemistry. Adolph (2019), on his part, investigated terminology in the fields of medicine and computers, originating from English in Swahili and the processes of their adaptation. His research findings clearly demonstrate that Swahili has expanded its vocabulary through the adaptation of medical and computer-related terms from English. Consequently, this adaptation has contributed to the growth of Swahili due to the significant expansion of scientific and technological vocabulary in the areas of computers and medicine. This expert states that one of the effects of adaptation is the increase in English terminology within Swahili, and thus 2 No. Strategy for Loan Translation of English Terminology into Swahili and Its Effects: An Analysis of Selected Entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary to meet the communication needs among members of the community. Language grows and changes every day according to the development of society. One of the main criteria for the growth and change of a language is the increase in terminology. According to Adolph (2019), in order for terminologies to increase in a language, new terms must be created. Terms are formed in a language so that its culture can accommodate concepts that were previously not part of that culture. This note is very important in this article as it shows how language grows and meets the communication needs among community members. This article examines the strategy of loan translation of English terminology into Swahili and its effects by focusing on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry, in contrast to Adolph's (2019) study, which investigates the development of the Swahili language through the adaptation of medical and computer terminology. Many scholars who have addressed borrowing agree that borrowing is the transfer of lexical elements from one language to another (Haugen, 1950; Polomé, 1980; Adolph, 2014; Winford, 2003). This article is divided into five sections: The first section is the introduction, in which the general concept of translation and its functions are explained, together with the concept of loan translation. The second section explains the theory that guided the analysis of the data in this article. The third section describes the methodology. The fourth section analyzes data on the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili and its effects. The discussion concerns terminology in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The fifth section is the conclusion. Theory  
The Theory of Scientific Terminology was used to provide data for this article. The Theory of Scientific Terminology is associated with Kiingi (1989), who is the original founder of this theory. Later, this theory was further developed by Kiingi (1992, 1998); Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001); Kevogo, Mukuthuria, and Ontieri (2018); and Kevogo (2020). This theory contains scientific criteria for effective terminology, which play a central role in the evaluation conducted in our article. Several scholars, such as Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008), have clearly outlined various principles that should be followed during the borrowing, adaptation, and formation of terminology from indigenous and foreign languages into Swahili. These principles are elaborated in Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008). This involves creating terminology using Swahili, Bantu languages, other African languages, and foreign languages. In addition to many other views expressed by Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (1997) regarding these principles, they recommend the following guidelines: Terminology should reflect the distinctive features of the concepts they represent (or at least suggest such features) and be clear to the intended users. If terminology is formed using compounding and word combination techniques, the following aspects must be considered:
The number of words combined or joined should not exceed two. Hyphens should not be used to separate compound terms, because in Swahili such terms are usually pronounced as a single word, with the primary stress on only one syllable. For example: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") and -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Such terms should not have more than four syllables, since Swahili words usually have an average of between one and five syllables. Terminology must be highly derivable in order to generate other related terms within the relevant domain or field. This will allow terms representing closely related or derivationally connected concepts to logically reflect that connection. For example: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), and -siyo wa taifa ("un-national"). Terminology (especially those with overlapping shades of meaning) must maintain consistency in sequence. The following terms, for example, demonstrate an acceptable alignment of sequence: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, and so on. Terminology must be adequate, meaning it should reflect the characteristics of the concepts they represent (and not, for instance, contradict them). For example, the term “tahakiki ya maandishi” is inappropriate because it generally refers to the evaluation of writing at large, rather than the analysis or critique of literature. Terminology must also be short and understandable. Lengthy terms, such as “majira ya majani kupukutika” (when the dry season approaches), are unsuitable because they do not adhere to the principle of linguistic economy. These principles are essential in terminology creation as they provide guidance on what should be done regarding borrowing, formation, and adaptation. In addition, methods for creating terminology have been proposed. Let us look at these methods below: first, translation, especially from languages known to be international, such as English, French, Spanish, and so on. Second, forming terminology based on conceptual frameworks. This theory is relevant as it provides the foundations to follow during the translation process. Likewise, it clarifies the methods of terminology creation. 

Methodology  
Every researcher uses appropriate and clear methods for their research. This article is the result of a descriptive research conducted both in the library and in the field. The researcher collected data from the Department of Foreign Languages and Linguistics, TATAKI from the University of Dar es Salaam, as well as BAKIZA in Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam Region, where data was gathered using interviews, questionnaires, and a library data source. According to Krishnaswami and Ranganatham (2005), interviews are a data collection method that involves an exchange between the researcher and the respondent with the aim of obtaining information related to the topic under investigation. Using the interview method, the researcher was able to conduct face-to-face interviews with translation experts from the aforementioned departments and institutions. A questionnaire is prepared with the aim of collecting important information from respondents (Mugenda and Mugenda, 2003). The questionnaire method can be conducted either face-to-face or through non-face-to-face means, depending on advancements in science and technology. Advancements in science and technology have facilitated the sending of various questionnaires by researchers to their respondents electronically (via web and email). However, the researcher of this article used face-to-face questionnaires because the informants were in the same location and easily accessible. In addition, the researcher reviewed various writings such as journals, dissertations, dictionaries, and so on from the library data source. Research Findings

The findings of this article were obtained after an investigation and analysis of data concerning the development of Swahili through the loan translation of terminology from English. Loan translation is a strategy for term creation involving word-for-word transfer of both structural elements and general concepts. The structure of terms created using the loan translation strategy changes to conform to the morphological and phonological rules of the target language. From the methods of interviews, questionnaires, and the library data source, it was found that several terms in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry—through the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012)—have been incorporated into Swahili from English via the loan translation strategy. The findings of this article indicate that terminology in biology, chemistry, and physics has been translated through the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili. This is due to the high demand for these terms among Swahili users, as well as the development and growth of science and technology. This situation compels Swahili to use the loan translation strategy in order to meet the communication needs of Swahili speakers and to incorporate concepts derived from these terms. Effects of Loan Translation The loan translation strategy has had various effects on different languages around the world, especially the Swahili language. Benefits for Language Translators and Global Recognition of TUKI

The strategy of borrowing English terms into Swahili through loan translation as a method for creating Swahili terminology has played a significant role in providing opportunities for language translators. For instance, TUKI (2012) has translated an adequate vocabulary related to the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry by employing the loan translation strategy and other forms of borrowing; however, this article focuses on the loan translation strategy. This institution has translated vocabulary from biology, physics, and chemistry from English into Swahili. Indeed, this work has brought global recognition to TUKI due to its great importance in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Alongside international recognition, those involved in this work have also benefited economically from sales made through published books, including the standardized Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary. This is attributed to the significance of its contents, the care taken in its preparation, and especially the expertise and professionalism of the dictionary’s compilers. This clearly demonstrates that its users have great confidence in this dictionary and are therefore willing to make purchases without hesitation. The Global Spread of the Swahili Language

Based on information from respondents (field data) as well as library data, the researcher has found that the loan translation strategy implemented by TUKI (2012) has contributed to the worldwide recognition of Swahili, since the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry are used globally due to advancements in science and technology, as well as their importance to students studying these subjects and to Swahili speakers in general. Furthermore, speakers of other languages apart from Swahili need to learn the vocabulary of these fields in the Swahili language. This situation leads them to acquire several Swahili language books, including this dictionary. All these factors have significantly contributed to the overall spread of Swahili throughout the world. The global spread of Swahili has encouraged people from various countries to learn Swahili, appreciate it, and value it highly.

Conclusion

The analysis in this article confirms the argument that the loan translation strategy has been used as one of the methods for borrowing English terminology into Swahili. The terms examined in this article are those from the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. In the case of biology, terms such as: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, biennial plants, nitrogen, occiput, spermatid, and zoology were identified. The researcher also considered the loan translation strategy in the field of chemistry. The following are some of the terms addressed in this field: absolute, acetate, active mass, masi tendaji, acylation, bond energy, pesticide, x-radiation, and zymology. Additionally, the researcher of this article has also examined the effects of the loan translation strategy on the Swahili language, language translators, students of biology, physics, and chemistry, speakers of other languages learning Swahili, and Swahili speakers in general. The findings of this article have revealed that this strategy has been beneficial to language translators, especially those translating from English into Swahili. A good example is the experts at TUKI who translated terms from these fields from English into Swahili. These translators have improved economically due to the global sale of this dictionary. It has also become evident that TUKI, which is now known as TATAKI, has become recognized and established worldwide. Introduction  
Translation is the act of transferring a message contained in writing from the source language to the target language without altering the intended meaning in the source language. Thus, translation is regarded as a method of learning foreign languages, showcasing various cultures, and transmitting the knowledge and skills of other communities, such as information on scientific and technological advancements. The motivation that drives a person to translate the message from the source language to the target language is the desire to facilitate communication among speakers of different languages. We can therefore say that translation is a means or even a bridge to bring together various communities that speak different languages. Moreover, loan translation is one method of coining new vocabulary, where a concept from the source language is adopted and translated into the target language; for example, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, and so on. The strategy of borrowing through loan translation has gained momentum due to the significant developments occurring in the field of science and technology, coupled with society’s advancement into modernity, resulting in a high demand for vocabulary to describe various concepts. The researcher of this article investigates the loan translation strategy of English vocabulary into Kiswahili.

This involves creating terminology using Swahili, Bantu languages, other African languages, and foreign languages. In addition to many other views expressed by Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (1997) regarding these principles, they recommend the following guidelines: Terminology should reflect the distinctive features of the concepts they represent (or at least suggest such features) and be clear to the intended users. If terminology is formed using compounding and word combination techniques, the following aspects must be considered:
The number of words combined or joined should not exceed two. Hyphens should not be used to separate compound terms, because in Swahili such terms are usually pronounced as a single word, with the primary stress on only one syllable. For example: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") and -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Such terms should not have more than four syllables, since Swahili words usually have an average of between one and five syllables. Terminology must be highly derivable in order to generate other related terms within the relevant domain or field. This will allow terms representing closely related or derivationally connected concepts to logically reflect that connection. For example: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), and -siyo wa taifa ("un-national").

Istilahi sharti ziwe toshelevu, yaani ziakisi sifa za dhana zinazoziwakilisha (na siyo, mathalani kupingana nazo) kwa mfano, istilahi: tahakiki ya maandishi si mwafaka kwa sababu inamaanisha uhakiki wa maandishi kwa jumla badala ya uhakiki au uchambuzi wa fasihi. discourses.translated_txt: Terminology (especially those with overlapping shades of meaning) must maintain consistency in sequence. The following terms, for example, demonstrate an acceptable alignment of sequence: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, and so on. Terminology must be adequate, meaning it should reflect the characteristics of the concepts they represent (and not, for instance, contradict them). For example, the term “tahakiki ya maandishi” is inappropriate because it generally refers to the evaluation of writing at large, rather than the analysis or critique of literature. Terminology must also be short and understandable. Lengthy terms, such as “majira ya majani kupukutika” (when the dry season approaches), are unsuitable because they do not adhere to the principle of linguistic economy.

Research Findings

The findings of this article were obtained after an investigation and analysis of data concerning the development of Swahili through the loan translation of terminology from English. Loan translation is a strategy for term creation involving word-for-word transfer of both structural elements and general concepts. The structure of terms created using the loan translation strategy changes to conform to the morphological and phonological rules of the target language. From the methods of interviews, questionnaires, and the library data source, it was found that several terms in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry—through the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012)—have been incorporated into Swahili from English via the loan translation strategy.

The Loan Translation Strategy of English Terms into Swahili and Its Effects: An Analysis of Selected Entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary

Benefits for Language Translators and Global Recognition of TUKI

The strategy of borrowing English terms into Swahili through loan translation as a method for creating Swahili terminology has played a significant role in providing opportunities for language translators. For instance, TUKI (2012) has translated an adequate vocabulary related to the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry by employing the loan translation strategy and other forms of borrowing; however, this article focuses on the loan translation strategy. This institution has translated vocabulary from biology, physics, and chemistry from English into Swahili. Indeed, this work has brought global recognition to TUKI due to its great importance in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Alongside international recognition, those involved in this work have also benefited economically from sales made through published books, including the standardized Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary. This is attributed to the significance of its contents, the care taken in its preparation, and especially the expertise and professionalism of the dictionary’s compilers.

The Global Spread of the Swahili Language

Based on information from respondents (field data) as well as library data, the researcher has found that the loan translation strategy implemented by TUKI (2012) has contributed to the worldwide recognition of Swahili, since the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry are used globally due to advancements in science and technology, as well as their importance to students studying these subjects and to Swahili speakers in general. Furthermore, speakers of other languages apart from Swahili need to learn the vocabulary of these fields in the Swahili language. This situation leads them to acquire several Swahili language books, including this dictionary. All these factors have significantly contributed to the overall spread of Swahili throughout the world. The global spread of Swahili has encouraged people from various countries to learn Swahili, appreciate it, and value it highly.

Conclusion

The analysis in this article confirms the argument that the loan translation strategy has been used as one of the methods for borrowing English terminology into Swahili. The terms examined in this article are those from the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. In the case of biology, terms such as: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, biennial plants, nitrogen, occiput, spermatid, and zoology were identified. The researcher also considered the loan translation strategy in the field of chemistry.
